factProposals.value: Relay runs in production on Fly.io: relay-qn (public read-only status at https://relay-qn.fly.dev/status, autoscaler and 1-3 worker processes on one 512MB machine) and relay-qn-redis (private Redis 7.4 with a password, append-only persistence on a 1GB volume).
Monitoring samples (success rate, p95 latency, DLQ, review, queue depth, workers) are stored every 60s in a capped Redis stream (relay:metrics, ~7 days) and served at /metrics/history.
Estimated running cost about $6-8/month; exactly one app machine, because the autoscaler runs in-process.

decisions.statement: The public HTTP surface is read-only; jobs are submitted from inside the deployment (fly ssh console + submitJobs).
decisions.rationale: no write endpoint means nothing to authenticate or abuse on a public URL, and the status page shows counts, never job content.

decisions.statement: Liveness (/health) has no dependencies; Redis reachability is a separate readiness check and is shown on the status page.
decisions.rationale: a Redis outage should be visible as 'down' to analysts, not cause Fly to restart-loop a healthy app.

decisions.statement: Production runs compiled JavaScript rather than tsx.
decisions.rationale: each worker is its own Node process; measured ~72MB server + ~64MB per worker compiled, so three workers fit a 512MB machine.
a job queue must never silently drop entries to free memory; a full Redis fails writes loudly instead.

decisions.statement: Circuit breaker trip frequency is recorded as null rather than 0.
decisions.rationale: the worker path makes no external calls, so there is no breaker to trip; 0 would claim a measurement that never happened.

limitations.statement: No alerting: problems are visible on the status page and in logs only.
Automatic rollback has only been exercised in its 'no previous image' branch (first deploy), not a deliberate bad-deploy drill.
Redis is a single machine with a volume, no replica; deploys run from a laptop (test-gated), no CI/CD.
